label: Mid/late original-phase steps (t 3-7) on m/i/p-like inputs, boosted when sequence starts with e/u
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at t=3..8, peaking at t=4-6 (98.6% of mass is in the original phase; it never fires at t<3 or in the copy phase, and fires weakly at <DEL>, 1.4%). Within that window it behaves like a soft conjunction of two things. (1) The current input token: m is by far the strongest (8.9x lift, 36% of mass, and m tops every top example), then i, p, l, r, a, x, o. (2) The first original token: e (5.8x) and u (4.3x), then g/q/c. The largest activations are m at t=4-6 in sequences that start with e or u. It favours the first occurrence of a token (in_first: 87% of mass). It does not fire on the first three tokens, during copying, or on most other letters and digits. The conjunction predicate gets about F1 0.42 on dev. Using only the t-window gives recall 0.97 but precision 0.04, so the activation looks like a graded mix of current token, first token and position that no crisp rule captures.
